Reylo is powered by TypeScript content mappers, introduced in TypeScript 7.1 (still in beta), which let you dynamically define static types for external file types and integrate them directly into TypeScript compilation.

Reylo is the perfect option for the agent era:

- 💪 The full power of SQL — any syntax, function or operator your database supports
- 🌵 DRY — no redundant hand-written types
- 🎯 Checked against your database — a misspelled column is a type error
- 🤖 Agent-friendly — DRY code is more maintainable for agents
- 🧩 Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and ClickHouse — Neon, PlanetScale, Cloudflare D1, Turso and more
- 🔌 Bring your own driver — pg , postgres.js, mysql2 , better-sqlite3 and more
- ⚡ No codegen — no generated files, no watcher

 Setup

To install Reylo, you'll need:

- TypeScript 7.1 (still in beta). The first release with content mappers. Install it with npm install -D typescript@next .
- Node 24 or later. 
- A running dev database. Postgres, MySQL 8.0.38 or later, ClickHouse 25.11 or later (in preview), or a SQLite file: Reylo reads your current schema from it.

For Bun, Nub, Vite, Next.js, esbuild, Rolldown, Rollup, webpack, Rspack, Cloudflare Workers and Jest, add the plugin for your setup, or copy its complete example project. To see the types as you type, set up your editor.

To give your coding agent Reylo's rules for writing and running queries, install its skill:

 

 Usage

Write a query in a .sql file, import it, and run it with your database driver:

 

 

Name each parameter with a colon, and give it a type with a cast where the query doesn't pin one down. Pass .run() your driver's client: a pool, a client, or a connection or transaction taken from one.

It resolves to the rows, shaped by how many the query can return:

 The query Resolves to 
 --- --- 
 A match on a primary or unique key, or limit 1 Row \ null 
 An aggregate without group by , a one-row insert … returning Row 
 An insert , update or delete without returning void 
 Anything else Row[] 

An imported query also has .runSync() , .try() , .readOnly , .with() , .sql , .raw and .source (Usage). Every query Reylo runs is published on Node's tracing channel reylo:query , for a tracer or a logger to subscribe to (Observability).

 What Reylo infers

To type a query, Reylo has your dev database prepare it, without running it, and reads back the type of every column and parameter. On top of that, it infers:

- Nulls — a column is nullable unless its schema, a join or a where test rules null out.
- Cardinality — a match on a unique key is one row or null , and an aggregate is exactly one row.
- Unions — an enum, or a column whose check constraint lists its values, is a union of them.
- JSON — JSON the query builds, and a JSON column with a JSON Schema check, keep their shape.

Each has examples in Inference.

 Supported drivers

Reylo is bring-your-own-driver. Pass .run() a client from any of these, or a Drizzle connection or Knex instance over one:

- Postgres — pg , postgres.js, Bun.sql , PGlite, Neon, pg-promise , slonik , @vercel/postgres , Drizzle Postgres
- MySQL — mysql2 , mariadb , PlanetScale, Bun.sql 
- SQLite — better-sqlite3 , node:sqlite , Bun.sql , libSQL, Turso, SQLite Wasm, sql.js, Cloudflare D1 and Durable Objects, sqlite3 , sqlite 
- ClickHouse (preview) — @clickhouse/client , @clickhouse/client-web 

 Documentation

reylo.dev/docs covers the rest: every plugin and editor, configuration, errors, each database's data types and edge cases, and Reylo Migrate for SQL-first schema migrations. Agents can read it all as Markdown at reylo.dev/llms.txt, or fetch any page with Accept: text/markdown . To move a Prisma project's queries to Reylo, see Migrating from Prisma.

intro.html:
Import .sql files into your TypeScript code with full type inference

Read the docs → · Try it in your browser →


If you have a file like this:

-- get_author.sql
select u.id, u.name, count(p.id)::int as post_count
from users u
left join posts p on p.user_id = u.id
where u.id = :id::int
group by u.id

You can import it directly from a TypeScript file like this:

// main.ts
import postgres from "postgres";
import getAuthor from "./get_author.sql";

const db = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL);

const author = await getAuthor.run(db, { id: 1 });
// { id: number; name: string; post_count: number } | null

install.title: Setup
install.html:
To install Reylo, you'll need:

  • TypeScript 7.1 (still in beta). The first release with content mappers. Install it with npm install -D typescript@next.
  • Node 24 or later.
  • A running dev database. Postgres, MySQL 8.0.38 or later, ClickHouse 25.11 or later (in preview), or a SQLite file: Reylo reads your current schema from it.

Install Reylo, which brings its engine for your machine, and TypeScript 7.1:

npm install reylo
npm install -D typescript@next

Add Reylo to tsconfig.json, for .sql files and for its project file, .reylo.yaml or .reylo.yml:

// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": { /* ... */ },
  "contentMappers": [{ "package": "reylo" }]
}

Then type-check with --runExternalCode, which lets tsc run content mappers:

// package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit --runExternalCode"
  }
}

Point Reylo at your dev database with DATABASE_URL, in your environment or in .env. Its scheme tells Reylo which database you use:

# .env
DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost:5432/app  # or mysql://… or sqlite:./path/to/your.db, etc

To make .sql imports work at run time too, load Reylo where your code runs. On Node:

node --env-file=.env --import reylo/register main.ts

For Bun, Nub, Vite, Next.js, esbuild, Rolldown, Rollup, webpack, Rspack, Cloudflare Workers and Jest, add the plugin for your setup, or copy its complete example project. To see the types as you type, set up your editor.

To give your coding agent Reylo's rules for writing and running queries, install its skill:

npx skills add reylosql/reylo --skill reylo
